quote: Publius Scipio was continued in command for a period not limited in point of time
notes: Senate prorogues Scipio's African command without time limit, until the war's end, an unusual open-ended grant (livy:en:30:1).

quote: they sent thirty of their principal elders as deputies to solicit peace
notes: Carthaginian polity, dismayed by Syphax's capture, silences the war party and sends thirty elders to Scipio to solicit peace and a truce (livy:en:30:16).

quote: They requested that the senate would by a decree confirm the title of king with the other favours and benefits conferred by Scipio
notes: Masinissa's envoys appeal to the senate, which confirms his royal title, decrees presents, and releases Numidian captives (livy:en:30:17).

quote: Caius Servilius should be indemnified for having filled the offices of plebeian tribune and plebeian aedile contrary to what was established by the laws
notes: A plebiscite retroactively indemnifies the consul Servilius for office-holding that violated the law because his curule father was alive in captivity (livy:en:30:19).

quote: ambassadors from Saguntum arrived, bringing with them some Carthaginians who had crossed over into Spain for the purpose of hiring auxiliaries
notes: Saguntine allies appeal to the senate with captured Carthaginian recruiters and their gold; senate imprisons the men, returns the treasure, and rewards the envoys (livy:en:30:21).

quote: The ambassadors were dismissed without having accomplished the peace, and almost without an answer
notes: Senate debates the first Carthaginian peace embassy; Laevinus's view that they are spies prevails and the envoys are dismissed (livy:en:30:21-23, quote at livy:en:30:23).

quote: Publius Sulpicius, who was created dictator for this very purpose, recalled the consul to Italy, in virtue of his superior authority
notes: Consul Servilius crosses to Sicily unauthorized hoping to invade Africa, so a dictator is created expressly to recall him by superior imperium (livy:en:30:24).

quote: the people were yelling in the vestibule of the senate-house, lest so great a booty should escape from their hands and their sight
notes: Carthaginian polity: a crowd besieges the senate-house and a mixed assembly of senate and people votes to seize storm-driven Roman transports despite the truce (livy:en:30:24).

quote: distributed to the people, so much for each street, at the rate of four asses a bushel, a great quantity of corn which had been sent out of Spain
notes: Curule aediles distribute Spanish grain street by street at four asses a bushel, cheap-grain politics rather than a dispute proper (livy:en:30:26).

quote: being engaged, according to a decree of the senate, in making inquisitions respecting the conspiracies of the principal inhabitants
notes: The consul is detained in Etruria conducting senate-decreed inquisitions into conspiracies of leading Etruscans (livy:en:30:26).

quote: All the tribes nominated Publius Scipio. Nevertheless, the consuls put the province of Africa to the lot, for so the senate had decreed
notes: Both consuls seek Africa to supersede Scipio; the tribes unanimously back Scipio yet the senate still has the consuls cast lots, giving Claudius equal command (livy:en:30:27).

quote: Hannibal, indignant that such language should be held and listened to at such a juncture, laid hold of Gisgo with his own hand, and dragged him from his elevated position
notes: Carthaginian polity: Hannibal forcibly drags the anti-peace speaker Gisgo from the rostrum, then apologizes and argues the terms are necessary (livy:en:30:37).

quote: having nominated Caius Servilius Geminus as dictator, that he might not be recalled to the city to hold the elections
notes: Consul Servilius names Servilius Geminus dictator to hold the elections so he need not leave his province (livy:en:30:39).

quote: fresh ones were not appointed to succeed them, the state was without curule magistrates
notes: Weather repeatedly blocks the elections, outgoing magistrates retire leaving no curule magistrates, and two plebeian aediles abdicate over a flaw in their election (livy:en:30:39).

quote: found, on the testimony of an informer, to have privately conveyed money out of the treasury, and were condemned, not without disgrace to the aedile Lucullus
notes: Aediles' scribes and runners are convicted on an informer's evidence of stealing treasury money, disgracing the aedile Lucullus (livy:en:30:39).

quote: He therefore refused to allow any business to be transacted before the province of Africa was assigned him
notes: Consul Lentulus obstructs all public business demanding Africa; tribunes resist, and after disputes in senate and assembly the senate votes a compromise under oath (livy:en:30:40).

quote: they were told, that the king was seeking occasion for war, and that if he persisted he would soon obtain his object
notes: Philip's ambassadors are heard and dismissed with a warning that the king has doubly violated the treaty (livy:en:30:42).

quote: Cneius Lentulus, whose province the fleet was, protested against the decree of the senate
notes: Consul Lentulus blocks the senate's peace decree; tribunes carry the question to the people, and all tribes order Scipio to grant the peace and bring home the army (livy:en:30:43).

quote: Now, because a tribute is to be levied from private property, you lament with one accord, as though at the funeral of the state
notes: Carthaginian polity: struggling to raise the first indemnity instalment from private property, the senate laments and Hannibal's laughter provokes Hasdrubal Haedus's rebuke (livy:en:30:44).

quote: He was, doubtless, the first general who was distinguished by a name derived from the nation which he had conquered
notes: Scipio triumphs with unparalleled splendour and receives the surname Africanus, the first commander ever surnamed from his conquest, setting an honorific precedent (livy:en:30:45).
